reason: The text contradicts this statement in multiple ways: (1) God's anger is explicitly directed against both Jerusalem AND Judah ('עַל־ אַף יְהוָה הָיְתָה בִירוּשָׁלִַם וּבִיהוּדָה' - 'the anger of Yahweh was against Jerusalem and Judah'), indicating judgment on the entire people, not special care for leaders; (2) God shows explicit mercy toward the common people by leaving some of the 'poor of the land' ('מִדַּלַּת הָאָרֶץ') as vinedressers and plowmen; (3) God demonstrates care for the people's welfare by appointing Gedaliah as governor and instructing them to dwell in the land and it will go well with them ('שְׁבוּ בָאָרֶץ וְעִבְדוּ אֶת־מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל וְיִטַב לָכֶם'); (4) The final act of kindness toward Jehoiachin is attributed to Evil-Merodach, not to Yahweh. The text demonstrates God's judgment on all Judah and mercy extended to the common people, not preferential care for leaders.
